title: Spanish Empire

endonym.native: Monarquía universal española(Monarquía hispánica /Monarquía de España /Monarquía española)

capsule: The Spanish Empire, forged after the Castilian crown's sponsorship of Columbus's 1492 voyage and the subsequent conquest of the Aztec (1521) and Inca (1532) empires, became the first global empire and the dominant world power of the 16th century. At its height under Philip II (r. 1556–1598) it included the Iberian Peninsula, the Americas from California to Patagonia, the Philippines, and parts of Italy and the Low Countries. Silver extracted from Potosí and Zacatecas financed European hegemony but also fueled inflation. The empire contracted through the 17th and 18th centuries as it lost the Netherlands, Jamaica, and other territories; the Spanish-American wars of independence (1810–1825) stripped it of nearly all its mainland American holdings, and the Spanish-American War of 1898 cost it Cuba, Puerto Rico, and the Philippines, ending the empire's attested span near 1879 in our dataset.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core colonial territories in the Americas and Philippines are well documented via viceregal administrative boundaries and papal demarcation lines; outer frontier zones (Amazonia, the Great Plains, Pacific Northwest) are conjectural; overall confidence is high for formally claimed territory, moderate for effective administrative control.
